evidence_items.publisher: arXiv — Gundlach, Lynch, Mertens and Thompson
evidence_items.locator: Section 6, 'Inference Costs Are Falling, but Overall Benchmarking Costs are Increasing'
evidence_items.explanation: The study's April 2024–November 2025 data show increasing frontier expenditure alongside longer reasoning and larger models. This supports the cost-escalation mechanism for frontier workloads, although its causal attribution is observational.

The analysis finds falling total inference expenditure at fixed benchmark scores, with halving times measured in months. This contradicts an unqualified rise in the cost of comparable performance, while remaining compatible with more spending on the frontier.

Zitron's linked source describes rising application spending from more tokens, larger contexts and reasoning. It does not provide a controlled historical comparison holding completed work and quality constant.

unresolved_gaps: No representative industry-wide task mix or cost measure is specified.
The measurements concern customer inference expenditure, not audited internal provider costs.
The frontier-cost study does not experimentally isolate reasoning-token growth from model size and demand for higher quality.
